steps.title: Open the modulation panel
steps.body: Ember has four LFOs, two envelopes, four followers, an XY pad, MIDI sources and eight macros. Everything cool-coloured in the interface is control rather than audio.

steps.title: Sources live here
steps.body: Each card shows what its source is doing right now. The XLFO is the one to start with: it has an editable shape rather than a fixed waveform.

steps.title: Drag a source onto a control
steps.body: Pick up an XLFO by its handle and drop it on Drive. The knob grows a cool ring showing the range the modulation covers and a dot showing where it is now.
steps.hint: Drop a source on a knob.

steps.title: Set the amount
steps.body: Alt-drag a modulated knob to change how far the modulation reaches, without moving the knob's own value. The ring shows the span; the dot shows the sum.

steps.title: Sync to tempo
steps.body: An LFO in sync mode follows the host's tempo in musical divisions. Free mode is in hertz and is what you want for anything that should not lock to the grid.

steps.title: The matrix view
steps.body: Every routing in one table, with its amount and curve, and a button to remove it. Faster than hunting for a knob when you have lost track of what is moving.
